newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia finances Q3 c/a deficit with debt.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia finances Q3 c/a deficit with debt.

text.p: Australia financed its A$5.68 billion September quarter current account deficit predominantly by borrowing, rather than selling equity, according to figures released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics on Tuesday.

Capital account figures showed Australia took on A$4.45 billion in additional net debt in the quarter, up from A$1.52 billion in the June quarter and compared with A$11.44 billion for the year to June (a quarterly average of A$2.86 billion).
Additional net equity liabilities amounted to A$1.06 billion in the September quarter, down from A$3.596 billion previously. The 1995/96 total was A$9.31 billion (A$2.33 billion a quarter).
An additional A$168 million change in "net other" liabilities in the September quarter made up the difference.
The current account balance must be reflected in changes to the capital account balance, showing the liabilities that accrue from trade and other income flows.
The A$4.45 billion additional net debt will appear in Wednesday's International Investment Position publication, the foreign debt figures.
Those figures will also include adjustments to reflect valuation changes, such as movements in the exchange rate.
